mainTopic: What must be covered or kept away before saying קריאת שמע (ערוה, צואה, urine, and waste containers), and holy objects in a bedroom
overview: This amud first finishes the discussion of urine by naming the case where the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי disagree. The גמרא then explains that the משנה's sunrise deadline for a בעל קרי fits רבי יהושע, because it describes the practice of the ותיקין. The משנה lets him say שמע covered by water, and the גמרא explains that this means murky water, which separates the heart from the ערוה. A ברייתא allows even clear water, and the גמרא rules that the heel touching the ערוה is forbidden but merely seeing it is permitted. רבא teaches that a see-through cover works for צואה, which only needs to be covered, but not for ערוה, which must not be seen. The גמרא adds rulings about spit, a sandal, a naked גוי, and how much water must be added to urine. It then discusses waste containers near a bed, settles which sage holds which view, and asks how high a bed may be off the ground. The amud ends with a story about a ספר תורה in a bedroom and the rule of כלי בתוך כלי, and רבא begins a ruling about a cloak that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The practical difference: urine moist enough to moisten other things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion by naming the case where the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי disagree: urine that is wet enough to make something else wet.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, the difference between them is in a case of urine that is moist enough to make other things moist.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing the previous topic. It points to the exact case where the two opinions about urine and saying שמע give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא asked what practical difference there is between the opinions about urine. The answer: the dispute is over whether the cutoff is 'טופח על מנת להטפיח' (wet enough to wet something else). The תנא קמא forbids saying שמע only while the urine is that wet. רבי יוסי forbids it as long as the urine is damp at all, even if it is not wet enough to wet other things.

keyTerms.meaning: Moist enough to moisten something else that touches it
There is a difference between them (the practical case where the opinions split)

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute about urine and קריאת שמע comes down to how wet the urine must be. The test case is 'טופח על מנת להטפיח'.
steps.confusionAlert: This line does not start a new topic. It is the final answer to a question asked before This amud begins, so read it as the end of the urine discussion.

phrases.english: And here, in a case where it is moist enough to moisten other things,
phrases.notes: 'Here' refers to our case of urine and קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: there is a difference between them.
phrases.notes: This is the practical case where the opinions give different rulings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא בְּטוֹפֵחַ עַל מְנָת לְהַטְפִּיחַ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question earlier about what practical difference exists between the opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The opinions differ over the threshold of 'טופח על מנת להטפיח'. The תנא קמא forbids only at that level of wetness. רבי יוסי forbids even when the urine is merely damp.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The difference between the opinions is the case of 'טופח על מנת להטפיח'.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about going down to immerse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה about a בעל קרי who goes to immerse and must judge whether he can get out and say שמע before sunrise.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he went down to immerse, if he is able to come up, cover himself, and recite שמע before sunrise, he should do so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes a man who goes to immerse because of a seminal emission. If he has time to come out, get dressed, and say שמע before sunrise, he should do that. The word 'כו׳' tells us the quote continues, and the important detail is 'before sunrise' (קודם הנץ החמה).

keyTerms.meaning: He went down to immerse (in a מקוה)
To come up out of the water

phrases.english: If he went down to immerse,
phrases.notes: He is a בעל קרי going to purify himself.

phrases.english: if he is able to come up, etc.
phrases.notes: Full text: come up, cover himself, and recite שמע before sunrise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever can get out of the water and say שמע before sunrise should do so.

steps.title: Does the משנה follow רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the unattributed משנה follows רבי אליעזר, since it requires saying שמע before sunrise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that the unattributed משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who said that the time for שמע lasts until sunrise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking whose opinion the משנה matches. Since it requires saying שמע before sunrise, it seems to follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פרק, רבי אליעזר held that the morning שמע must be said by sunrise. רבי יהושע held that one has until the third hour. Since the משנה uses sunrise as the deadline, it looks like רבי אליעזר. That would be a problem, because the הלכה follows רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test)
The תנא who holds the morning שמע must be said by sunrise

steps.confusionAlert: 'לימא' is a suggestion, not a conclusion. Usually the גמרא raises it in order to reject it, as it does in the next step.

phrases.english: Shall we say that the תנא taught the unattributed משנה
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה.

phrases.english: in accordance with רבי אליעזר,
who said: until sunrise?
phrases.notes: The deadline for the morning שמע in his view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference about authorship from the 'before sunrise' detail in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה is following רבי אליעזר's sunrise deadline for שמע.

steps.title: It can follow רבי יהושע and describe the practice of the ותיקין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The משנה can follow רבי יהושע and be speaking about people who follow the custom of the ותיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי יהושע. Perhaps the משנה is speaking about those who act like the ותיקין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from the previous step. Sunrise in the משנה need not be the legal deadline. It may describe the ideal practice of extra-careful people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע agrees that one may say שמע until the third hour, so sunrise is not the legal cutoff. But the ותיקין chose to say שמע right at sunrise. The משנה may simply describe someone who wants to keep that higher standard, so it does not prove it follows רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (introduces a rejection)
Exceptionally careful, pious people who did מצוות at the ideal time
The תנא who allows the morning שמע until the third hour

steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the משנה in line with רבי יהושע, whose view is the הלכה. It also shows that a משנה can describe an ideal practice rather than the minimum requirement.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows רבי יהושע,
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע holds the deadline is the third hour.

phrases.english: perhaps it is speaking about those who follow the custom of the ותיקין.
phrases.notes: They said שמע at sunrise as a higher standard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the sunrise detail proves the משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Sunrise may be the ideal practice of the ותיקין, not the legal deadline.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the ותיקין finished שמע at sunrise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's statement that the ותיקין would finish שמע exactly at sunrise, which supports the previous step.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: The ותיקין would finish it (קריאת שמע) together with sunrise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the previous step with a source showing that the ותיקין timed שמע to sunrise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reports that the ותיקין timed שמע to end at sunrise, so they could go straight into תפילה at sunrise. This explains why the משנה would care about sunrise even under רבי יהושע: it is speaking about a person who wants to act like the ותיקין.

keyTerms.meaning: Together with, at the same moment as

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's sunrise detail fits רבי יהושע because it describes the ותיקין's practice of finishing שמע at sunrise.

phrases.english: As רבי יוחנן said:
The ותיקין would finish it
together with sunrise.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וָתִיקִין הָיוּ גּוֹמְרִין אוֹתָהּ עִם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the ותיקין practice mentioned in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: That the ותיקין timed שמע to sunrise.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement about the ותיקין.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: if not, cover in the water and recite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: if he cannot get out in time, he covers himself in the water and says שמע there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if not, he should cover himself in the water and recite.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no time to come out and dress before sunrise, the משנה lets him stay in the water. The water acts as his covering, and he says שמע there. The גמרא will now question whether water is really enough of a covering.

keyTerms.meaning: He should cover himself with the water

phrases.english: And if not,
phrases.notes: If he cannot get out and dress in time.

phrases.english: he should cover himself in the water and recite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next ruling in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who cannot get out in time may cover himself in the water and say שמע.

steps.title: But his heart sees his nakedness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: in clear water, nothing separates his heart from his nakedness, so how can he say שמע?
steps.simpleTranslation: But his heart sees his nakedness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling from the previous step. Water alone does not seem to block the heart from 'seeing' the ערוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that one may not say שמע when there is no separation between the heart and the ערוה (לבו רואה את הערוה). In clear water nothing physically divides the upper and lower body. So the water covering seems not to be enough. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: His heart 'sees' his nakedness: no separation between the heart and the ערוה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Seeing' here is not about eyesight. It means there is no barrier between the heart and the ערוה, which makes saying שמע forbidden.

phrases.english: But his heart sees his nakedness!
phrases.notes: Water does not separate the two parts of the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling that he may say שמע while covered by water.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one may say שמע while covered in water.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water does not create a barrier between the heart and the ערוה, and שמע is forbidden when 'לבו רואה את הערוה'.

steps.title: The משנה means murky water
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר (or רבי אחא בר אבא בר אחא in the name of רב) answers that the משנה is talking about murky water, which counts like solid earth and covers the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said, and some say it was רבי אחא בר אבא בר אחא in the name of our teacher רב: The משנה was taught about murky water. Murky water is like solid ground, so his heart does not see his nakedness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 7. The משנה is not talking about clear water at all. It means murky water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that clear water does not separate the heart from the ערוה. The answer is that murky water blocks the view, just as solid earth would. So the משנה's case has a real separation, and saying שמע is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you say' — here it means 'some say it was' a different אמורא who said this
'Our teacher' — in בבל this refers to רב
'They taught' — the law was said about this specific case
Murky, cloudy water that you cannot see through

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא בַּר אַחָא
phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Aha bar Abba bar Aha
in the name of our teacher (Rav):
phrases.notes: Two possible names for who reported this answer.

phrases.english: They taught this about murky water,
which is like solid earth,
so that his heart does not see his nakedness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7 by narrowing the משנה's case to murky water.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) — the משנה speaks only about murky water
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to allow saying שמע in any water, even clear water, where nothing separates the heart from the ערוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks about murky water, which counts as a separation like solid earth.

steps.title: A ברייתא about clear water
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that in clear water one sits up to his neck and says שמע. יש אומרים says he must first stir up the water with his foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: In clear water, he sits in it up to his neck and recites קריאת שמע. יש אומרים: he must make the water cloudy with his foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the same topic. The first opinion seems to allow saying שמע even in clear water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא has two opinions. The תנא קמא says sitting in water up to the neck is enough, even if the water is clear. The יש אומרים say clear water is not enough, so he must stir it with his foot to make it murky. This sets up the next questions on the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Clear water that you can see through
'Some say' — a second opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Clear water —
he sits in it up to his neck and recites (Shema).
And some say: he makes it cloudy with his foot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא. The יש אומרים fits Step 8 (murky water needed). The תנא קמא seems to disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: one may say שמע in clear water while sitting up to his neck. יש אומרים: he must make the water murky with his foot.

steps.title: Doesn't the heart see the nakedness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks on the תנא קמא: in clear water, the heart 'sees' the ערוה, so how can he say שמע?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the תנא קמא: but his heart sees the ערוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first opinion in the ברייתא. In clear water, nothing separates the heart from the ערוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same problem that was asked on the משנה in Step 7. The משנה could be explained as murky water, but the תנא קמא clearly speaks about clear water. So how does he allow it?

keyTerms.meaning: The first תנא — the first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: And according to the first Tanna,
but his heart sees the nakedness!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנָא קַמָּא, וַהֲרֵי לִבּוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תנא קמא of the ברייתא in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's ruling that one may say שמע in clear water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Clear water does not block the view. So the heart 'sees' the ערוה, which should forbid saying שמע.

steps.title: The תנא קמא allows it when the heart sees
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that when the heart 'sees' the ערוה, it is still permitted to say שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that if his heart sees the nakedness, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא simply holds that the heart seeing the ערוה is not a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed everyone agrees the heart may not 'see' the ערוה. The answer is that the תנא קמא disagrees with that rule. This is exactly where he argues with the יש אומרים, who require stirring the water.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Sees' — here it means facing the ערוה with nothing in between

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר לִבּוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: He holds: if his heart sees the nakedness — it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different underlying view — the תנא קמא does not accept the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone forbids saying שמע when the heart 'sees' the ערוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא permits it even when the heart sees the ערוה.

steps.title: Doesn't the heel see the nakedness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again: when sitting in clear water, his heel is facing the ערוה. Isn't that a problem?
steps.simpleTranslation: But his heel sees the nakedness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to the תנא קמא. When a person sits, his heel faces the ערוה with nothing in between.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the heart is fine, there may be a separate problem with the heel. When a person sits up to his neck, his heels come close to his private parts. In clear water nothing separates them.

phrases.english: But his heel sees the nakedness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge on the same תנא קמא, now about the heel.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's ruling in clear water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sitting in clear water, the heel faces the ערוה with no separation, which should forbid saying שמע.

steps.title: The תנא קמא allows it when the heel sees
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא also holds that when the heel 'sees' the ערוה, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that if his heel sees the nakedness, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer: the תנא קמא holds that the heel seeing the ערוה is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer has the same shape as Step 11. The תנא קמא is lenient both about the heart and about the heel. This leniency about the heel leads into the next discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: The heel faces the private parts with nothing in between

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר עֲקֵבוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: He holds: if his heel sees the nakedness, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר עֲקֵבוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different underlying view — the תנא קמא is lenient
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The heel 'seeing' the ערוה forbids saying שמע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא permits saying שמע even when the heel sees the ערוה.

steps.title: אביי and רבא argue about the heel touching
steps.stepSummary: It was stated: the heel seeing the ערוה is permitted. If the heel touches it, אביי forbids and רבא permits. This is how רב זביד taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if his heel sees the ערוה, it is permitted. If it touches — אביי said it is forbidden, and רבא said it is permitted. רב זביד taught this teaching this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of the אמוראים about the heel. In this version, everyone allows seeing, and the argument is only about touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 taught that the heel seeing is permitted. Now we learn that אביי and רבא argue about a stronger case, when the heel actually touches the ערוה. The גמרא notes that this is רב זביד's version, which prepares us for a second version.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was stated' — introduces a teaching of the אמוראים
Teaches, reports a teaching in a certain form

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר: עֲקֵבוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: It was stated: if his heel sees the nakedness, it is permitted;
if it touches — Abaye said: it is forbidden,
and Rava said: it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: רַב זְבִיד מַתְנִי לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא הָכִי.
phrases.english: Rav Zevid taught this teaching this way.
phrases.notes: Signals that another version is coming.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: עֲקֵבוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 13's rule about the heel and adds a מחלוקת about touching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב זביד's version: heel seeing is permitted by all. Heel touching is debated: אביי forbids, רבא permits.

steps.title: A second version of the argument
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בריה דרב איקא teaches it differently: touching is forbidden by everyone, and the argument is about seeing. רבא permits seeing because 'the Torah was not given to the ministering angels.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בריה דרב איקא taught it this way: If the heel touches, everyone agrees it is forbidden. If it sees, אביי said it is forbidden and רבא said it is permitted, because the תורה was not given to the מלאכי השרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same מחלוקת. In this version the argument moves to an easier case: the heel only seeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב זביד's version, touching was argued about and seeing was allowed. In this version, touching is forbidden by all, and even seeing is argued about. רבא's reason is that the Torah does not demand the impossible. People have bodies and cannot always avoid this, unlike angels.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah was not given to the ministering angels — it was given to real people with human limits

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In רב זביד's version the argument is about touching. In רב חיננא's version touching is forbidden by all, and the argument is only about seeing.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle לא נתנה תורה למלאכי השרת is a famous idea: הלכה is built for real human beings and does not demand what people cannot do.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא מַתְנִי לַהּ הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Hinnana, son of Rav Ika, taught it this way:
if it touches — everyone agrees it is forbidden;
if it sees — Abaye said: it is forbidden,
Rava said: it is permitted:
the Torah was not given to the ministering angels.
phrases.notes: רבא's reason: people cannot avoid this.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא מַתְנִי לַהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the מחלוקת from Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חיננא's version: touching is forbidden by all. For seeing, אביי forbids and רבא permits, since the Torah was not given to angels.

steps.title: The final ruling: touching forbidden, seeing permitted
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that if the heel touches the ערוה it is forbidden, and if it only sees it, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: if it touches, it is forbidden; if it sees, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling for this discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching is forbidden, which matches everyone in רב חיננא's version and אביי in רב זביד's version. Seeing is permitted, which matches רבא in רב חיננא's version and everyone in רב זביד's version. So the הלכה takes the stricter side on touching and the lenient side on seeing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the הלכה is' — the final practical ruling

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case of saying שמע in water refers to murky water. The תנא קמא of the ברייתא allows even clear water. The final הלכה about the heel: touching the ערוה is forbidden, seeing it is permitted.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: if it touches — it is forbidden;
if it sees — it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the practical הלכה after the two versions of the מחלוקת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The heel touching the ערוה forbids saying שמע. The heel only seeing the ערוה is permitted.

steps.title: רבא: A see-through cover works for צואה but not for ערוה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if צואה is behind a clear, glass-like cover, you may say קריאת שמע facing it. If ערוה is behind such a cover, you may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if צואה is inside a transparent lantern-like cover, it is permitted to say קריאת שמע facing it. If ערוה is behind such a cover, it is forbidden to say קריאת שמע facing it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבא that compares two unclean things behind a clear cover. One is allowed and one is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A עששית is a cover you can see through, like glass. רבא says it is enough for צואה but not enough for ערוה. The next step explains why the two are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A lantern or glass-like cover that you can see through

phrases.english: Rava said: feces inside a lantern-like (transparent) cover,
it is permitted to recite Shema facing it.
Nakedness behind a lantern-like cover,
it is forbidden to recite Shema facing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of the heel seeing ערוה to a new ruling about see-through coverings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A see-through cover is enough for צואה but not for ערוה.

steps.title: The reasons: feces needs covering, nakedness must not be seen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רבא's two rulings and gives each its reason from the פסוקים. For צואה the rule depends on being covered, and it is covered. For ערוה the rule depends on not being seen, and it can be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: צואה behind a clear cover is allowed, because for צואה everything depends on it being covered, and here it is covered. ערוה behind a clear cover is forbidden, because רחמנא said 'and no ערות דבר shall be seen among you', and here it can be seen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבא's words and explains the reason behind each half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rules come from two different פסוקים with two different key words. For צואה the פסוק says 'cover', so a glass cover counts as covered. For ערוה the פסוק says 'shall not be seen', so a glass cover fails because you can still see through it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
It is being seen, it is visible

steps.whatToRemember: צואה needs to be covered, so a clear cover is fine. ערוה must not be seen, so a clear cover is not enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in גמרא: the exact word in the פסוק ('cover' or 'seen') decides the practical law.

phrases.aramaic: צוֹאָה בַּעֲשָׁשִׁית מוּתָּר לִקְרוֹת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע כְּנֶגְדָּהּ
phrases.english: Feces in a lantern, it is permitted to recite Shema facing it,
because with feces, the matter depends on covering,
and here it is covered.

phrases.aramaic: עֶרְוָה בַּעֲשָׁשִׁית אָסוּר לִקְרוֹת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע כְּנֶגְדָּהּ,
phrases.english: Nakedness in a lantern, it is forbidden to recite Shema facing it,

phrases.aramaic: ״וְלֹא יִרְאֶה בְךָ עֶרְוַת דָּבָר״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא.
phrases.english: the Torah said: 'And no indecent thing shall be seen among you.'
And here it is visible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reason for each half of רבא's ruling in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צואה follows 'cover' and is covered. ערוה follows 'not seen' and is seen.

steps.title: אביי: A tiny bit of צואה can be canceled with spit
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that a very small amount of צואה can be covered and canceled by spitting on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: a tiny amount of צואה can be canceled with spit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling about covering צואה. אביי says spit can cover a small amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the rule for צואה depends on covering, even spit can work as a cover when the amount is tiny. Once it is covered this way, one may say קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: Any small amount, a tiny bit
He cancels it, makes it count as nothing

phrases.english: Abaye said: a tiny amount of feces,
one can cancel it with spit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that for צואה, covering is what matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small amount of צואה can be covered and canceled with spit.

steps.title: רבא: Only with thick spit
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a condition to אביי's ruling: the spit must be thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: and only with thick spit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows אביי's ruling by adding one condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thin, watery spit does not really cover anything. Thick spit actually hides the צואה, so only thick spit counts as a cover.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And', which here adds a condition to the earlier ruling

phrases.english: Rava said: and with thick spit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to אביי's ruling in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only thick spit cancels a small amount of צואה.

steps.title: רבא: Cover צואה in a hole with your sandal
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if צואה is in a small hole in the ground, one may place his sandal over the hole and then say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if צואה is in a hole, he puts his sandal on top of it and says קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another practical way to cover צואה: put a sandal over it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the rule for צואה is about covering. A sandal over the hole is a good enough cover, so one may say קריאת שמע there.

keyTerms.meaning: A small hole or pit in the ground

phrases.english: Rava said: feces in a hole,
he places his sandal on top of it,
and recites Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another application of the principle that צואה only needs to be covered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sandal placed over צואה in a hole is a valid cover.

steps.title: What if feces is stuck to the sandal?
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא asks about a case where צואה is stuck to his sandal. Is that a problem for saying קריאת שמע?
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא asked: if צואה is stuck to his sandal, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Following the sandal case, a sage asks a new question that is an opposite twist: what if the צואה is on the sandal itself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21 the sandal covered the צואה. Here the צואה is stuck to the sandal he is wearing. The question is whether it counts as covered, since it is under his foot, or whether he is considered dirty because it is attached to him.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question of law)

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, asked:
feces stuck to his sandal, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a related sandal case after רבא's ruling in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether צואה stuck to one's sandal prevents saying קריאת שמע.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו, meaning the question is left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not find an answer to the sandal question and leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found either way. The question about צואה stuck to a sandal stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'yes' or 'no'. It means the גמרא could not decide.

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 22 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question about צואה stuck to a sandal is left unresolved.

steps.title: רב יהודה: No קריאת שמע facing a naked גוי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that it is forbidden to say קריאת שמע facing a naked גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: it is forbidden to say קריאת שמע facing a naked גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of ערוה with a new ruling from רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nakedness of a גוי also counts as ערוה for קריאת שמע. The next steps ask why רב יהודה needed to mention a גוי specifically.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
a naked gentile,
it is forbidden to recite Shema facing him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the laws of covering צואה back to the laws of ערוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The nakedness of a גוי is ערוה, and one may not say קריאת שמע facing it.

steps.title: Why mention a gentile? A Jew is the same!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב יהודה said 'a גוי', since facing a naked Jew is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically a גוי? Even a Jew is also forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב יהודה: why did he single out a גוי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a naked Jew is also forbidden, then saying 'גוי' seems pointless or misleading. The גמרא wants to know what the word 'גוי' teaches us.

phrases.english: Why specifically a gentile?
Even a Jew is also forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רב יהודה's ruling in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'גוי' in רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same law applies to a Jew, so naming a גוי specifically seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A Jew is obvious; a gentile needed to be taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: a Jew is obviously forbidden. רב יהודה needed to teach the case of a גוי, because one might think a גוי's body is compared to a donkey's and is not ערוה. The פסוק about נח's sons shows that a non-Jew's nakedness is also called ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a Jew, it is obvious that it is forbidden. He needed to teach about a גוי. You might have said: since it is written about them 'whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys', a גוי is like a mere donkey. So he teaches us that they too are called ערוה, as it is written: 'and their father's nakedness they did not see.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב יהודה mentioned a גוי. It was to reject a possible mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea (מהו דתימא) comes from a פסוק in יחזקאל that compares them to donkeys, which would suggest no ערוה at all. The proof against it is that the Torah calls נח's nakedness ערוה, and נח was not Jewish. So a non-Jew's nakedness is real ערוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh of donkeys (from a פסוק in יחזקאל)

steps.whatToRemember: The nakedness of a non-Jew is also ערוה. We learn this from נח, whose nakedness the Torah calls ערוה.

phrases.english: A Jew, it is obvious to him that it is forbidden,
but a gentile, he needed to state.
You might have said,
since it is written about them:
'whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys,'
say he is like a mere donkey;
so he teaches us
that they too are called 'nakedness,'
as it is written: 'And their father's nakedness they did not see.'

steps.triggerLanguage: יִשְׂרָאֵל פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּאָסוּר, אֶלָּא גּוֹי אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 by showing why the case of a גוי needed to be taught.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Necessity of the teaching (איצטריך) to reject a possible mistake.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a פסוק compares them to donkeys, a גוי's nakedness might not count as ערוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah calls נח's nakedness ערוה, so a גוי's nakedness is ערוה too.

steps.title: The משנה: Do not cover yourself with foul water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: one may not cover himself with foul water or flax-soaking water until he pours fresh water into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he may not cover himself with foul water or with water used for soaking flax until he pours water into them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to say that foul water becomes acceptable once you add clean water to it. The next step questions whether that reading makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Water used for soaking flax, which smells very bad

phrases.english: And he may not cover himself, not with foul water
and not with flax-soaking water
until he pours water into them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to examine its next line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As it seems at first: foul or flax water becomes usable once clean water is added.

steps.title: How much water would he have to keep pouring?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how much water can he keep pouring in? It is not practical to fix such a large amount of foul water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much water would he have to keep pouring in?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the simple reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To cover himself, the person needs a large pool of water. Fixing that much foul water would take an endless amount of clean water, so the plain reading of the משנה seems impossible.

phrases.english: And how much water does he keep pouring in?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the simple reading of the משנה quoted in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'until he pours water into them' as applied to foul and flax water.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fixing enough foul water to cover oneself would take an impractical amount of clean water.

steps.title: Re-reading the משנה: foul water never, urine with added water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads the משנה. Foul water and flax water may never be used as a cover. Adding water only works for urine, and then he may say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: he may not cover himself with foul water or flax water at all. And urine, until he pours water into it, and then he may recite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by splitting the משנה's line into two separate rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'until he pours water' do not go with foul water or flax water. Those are never allowed. The words go with urine, which a small amount of added water can fix.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it means (re-reading the text)

steps.whatToRemember: Foul water and flax water can never serve as a cover for קריאת שמע. Urine becomes acceptable once clean water is added.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'until he pours water' as fixing foul water. After the re-reading, it applies only to urine.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it says:
he may not cover himself, not with foul water
and not with flax-soaking water, at all.
And urine,
until he pours water into it, and then he may recite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 by re-reading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading of the משנה (הכי קאמר), splitting it into two rules.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Adding water fixes foul water and flax water.
steps.terutzMaskana: Foul water and flax water are never allowed. Adding water fixes only urine.

steps.title: A disagreement about how much water to add
steps.stepSummary: A בָּרַיְיתָא gives two amounts for water added to urine: any amount, or a רְבִיעִית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: How much water must one add to it? Any amount. רבי זכאי says: A quarter-log.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a בָּרַיְיתָא that puts a number on the water mentioned in the previous step. It records two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view accepts even a tiny amount of water. רבי זכאי requires a רְבִיעִית; the next steps will ask when each amount is required.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who requires a quarter-log

phrases.english: The Sages taught: How much should he pour
water into it? Any amount.
Rabbi Zakkai says: A quarter-log.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כַּמָּה יָטִיל לְתוֹכָן מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Specifies how much water the previous step's rule requires.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view permits any amount of added water; רבי זכאי requires a רְבִיעִית.

steps.title: רב נחמן distinguishes water added afterward from water already present
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן limits the disagreement to adding water after the urine is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The disagreement concerns adding water afterward. But if water was there first, any amount suffices.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains which order of events the disagreement covers. He says the views disagree only when water is added after the urine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If clean water was in the vessel first, he says both views accept any amount. The order matters because the urine enters water that is already there.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: The disagreement is about adding water afterward.
But if the water was there first, any amount suffices.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the disagreement in the בָּרַיְיתָא to one order of events.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב נחמן, the views disagree when water is added afterward; when water was present first, any amount suffices.

steps.title: רב יוסף places the disagreement in the opposite case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the views disagree when water was present first, but require a רְבִיעִית when it is added afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: The disagreement concerns water put there first. But afterward, everyone agrees that a רביעית is required.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different way to place the disagreement. He says it concerns water put in before the urine, not water added afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For water added afterward, רב יוסף says everyone requires a רְבִיעִית. This reverses which case רב נחמן said had an agreed-upon answer.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage giving the second explanation
at the outset; here, before the urine enters

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said: The disagreement is about water present at the outset.
But if water is added afterward, everyone agrees that a quarter-log is required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite placement of the disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יוסף, the views disagree when water is present first; if it is added afterward, all require a רְבִיעִית.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks for a quarter-log of water
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells his attendant to bring a רְבִיעִית of water, following רבי זכאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to his attendant: Bring me a רביעית of water, following רבי זכאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what רב יוסף asked his attendant to bring. His request shows that he chose the amount required by רבי זכאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף has just said that the amount can be disputed when water is prepared first. He asks for a רְבִיעִית, the larger amount in that disagreement.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to his attendant:
Bring me a quarter-log of water,
in accordance with Rabbi Zakkai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the amount רב יוסף chose after explaining the disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף requests a רְבִיעִית, following רבי זכאי.

steps.title: An empty waste container still prevents reading opposite it
steps.stepSummary: A new בָּרַיְיתָא prohibits קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע opposite containers used for feces or urine, even when empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: One may not recite קריאת שמע opposite a container for צואה or a vessel for urine, even if they contain nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another בָּרַיְיתָא, now about the containers themselves. It says they remain a problem even when empty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is different from asking how to dilute urine. The rule here concerns a vessel used for waste, even when no waste is currently inside it.

keyTerms.term: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן כְּלוּם
keyTerms.meaning: even though there is nothing in them

phrases.english: The Sages taught: A container for feces
and a vessel for urine—
one may not recite Shema opposite them,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: even though they contain nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי וְעָבִיט שֶׁל מֵי רַגְלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the amount of water to the separate issue of waste containers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not recite קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע opposite these containers, even when empty.

steps.title: The new teaching repeats the water rule for urine itself
steps.stepSummary: The בָּרַיְיתָא distinguishes urine itself from an empty container and repeats the disagreement about added water.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for urine itself, water must be poured into it. How much? Any amount; רבי זכאי says a רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The בָּרַיְיתָא now turns from containers to urine itself. It explicitly repeats the two amounts stated earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding water addresses the urine. The earlier ruling about an empty waste container is a separate rule, so this line does not say that added water fixes the container itself.

phrases.english: And as for urine itself—
one must pour water into it.
And how much water should he pour into it?
Any amount.
Rabbi Zakkai says: A quarter-log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Distinguishes urine itself from the containers just discussed and repeats the earlier amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water may address urine itself; the two stated amounts are any amount and a רְבִיעִית.

steps.title: The stated rule applies on either side of the bed
steps.stepSummary: The בָּרַיְיתָא says its preceding rule holds whether the item is in front of or behind the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether it is in front of the bed or behind the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: This short line adds a location detail to the rule just stated. It sets up the next view, which treats the two sides differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, merely putting the item behind the bed does not change the stated rule. The bed's position will become the point of disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: whether; used here for both cases

phrases.english: Whether in front of the bed
or behind the bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין לִפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה בֵּין לְאַחַר הַמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds where the item is located and prepares for the competing location rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The preceding rule applies both in front of and behind the bed.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל distinguishes the two sides of the bed
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits reading behind the bed but requires a distance of four אַמּוֹת in front of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Behind the bed, one may recite; in front of the bed, one may not, but one may move four אמות away and recite.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with treating both sides alike. He permits reading when the item is behind the bed, but requires distance when it is in front.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bed's position now changes the result. In the front-of-bed case, moving four אַמּוֹת away provides a way to read.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who distinguishes the two sides of the bed

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Behind the bed, one may recite;
in front of the bed, one may not recite,
but one moves four cubits away
and recites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the preceding rule's equal treatment of both sides of the bed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Behind the bed one may recite; in front of it one must first move four אַמּוֹת away.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר requires removal or placement beneath the bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does not permit reading merely because the room is large; the item must be removed or placed under the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Even in a house one hundred אמות long, one may not recite until one removes them or places them beneath the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives a stricter location rule. Even a very large room is not enough by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His stated solutions are to take the items out or put them under the bed. The size of the room alone does not provide permission to read.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage requiring removal or placement under the bed
a house one hundred cubits long

steps.whatToRemember: Keep the two issues separate: added water addresses urine itself, while a container used for waste has its own rule. The final views then disagree about how the bed's position affects reading nearby.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Even in a house one hundred cubits long—
one may not recite until one removes them
or places them beneath the bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a stricter alternative to relying on position behind the bed or the room's size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not recite until the items are removed or placed beneath the bed.

steps.title: What does the bed permit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to read the earlier ruling about a container behind or in front of the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was the ruling that someone may read immediately when the container is behind the bed, but must move four אַמּוֹת away when it is in front? Or must they move four אַמּוֹת away even when it is behind the bed, and not read at all when it is in front?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out two possible meanings of the earlier ruling. It has not yet decided which meaning is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how much protection the bed provides. In the first reading, the bed allows immediate reading from behind it; in the second, distance is still required.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised for them

phrases.english: A question was raised for them: What does he mean?
Behind the bed—he reads immediately,

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה — מַרְחִיק אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְקוֹרֵא,
phrases.english: in front of the bed—he moves four cubits away and reads?
Or perhaps this is what he means:

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר הַמִּטָּה — מַרְחִיק אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְקוֹרֵא,
phrases.english: Behind the bed—he moves four cubits away and reads,
in front of the bed—he does not read at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the wording of the earlier ruling attributed to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does placing the container behind the bed permit immediate reading, or is a distance of four אַמּוֹת still required?

steps.title: A second teaching states the bed rule clearly
steps.stepSummary: Another בָּרַיְיתָא explicitly permits immediate reading behind the bed, though it attributes that view to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that behind the bed one reads immediately, while in front of it one moves four אַמּוֹת away. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that even in a room one hundred אַמּוֹת long, one may not read until the containers are removed or put under the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another בָּרַיְיתָא to settle the two possible readings. Its wording clearly gives an immediate-reading rule for behind the bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This supports the first reading of the disputed wording. But the named sages are assigned the opposite views from the earlier בָּרַיְיתָא, so the new source also creates a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; an introduction to a source
A room one hundred cubits long

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Behind the bed—he reads immediately,
in front of the bed—he moves four cubits away.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even in a room one hundred cubits long—
he may not read until he removes them
or places them under the bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies an explicit version of the first possibility raised in step 39.
steps.raayaObject: Behind the bed, the rule permits reading immediately.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The new בָּרַיְיתָא explicitly says, “אַחַר הַמִּטָּה — קוֹרֵא מִיָּד.”

steps.title: The wording is clear, but the names conflict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the original question is answered, identifies a contradiction between the two בָּרַיְיתוֹת, and proposes reversing the names in the later one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our question has been resolved, but the teachings contradict each other. Reverse the later teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא separates two issues: what the rule says, and which sage says it. It proposes correcting the second בָּרַיְיתָא’s attribution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immediate reading behind the bed is now stated clearly. The remaining problem is that the two בָּרַיְיתוֹת attach the differing views to different sages; swapping the names in the later one would make them agree.

phrases.english: Our question has been resolved,
but the teachings contradict each other:
Reverse the later teaching.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מסקנא for the resolved wording; the step as a whole ends with a proposed answer to the contradiction.
steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעְיָין אִיפְּשִׁיטָא לַן, מַתְנְיָיתָא קַשְׁיָין אַהֲדָדֵי: אֵיפוֹךְ בָּתְרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The new בָּרַיְיתָא resolves the wording question but exposes conflicting attributions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reverse the sages’ attributions in the later בָּרַיְיתָא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Keep both בָּרַיְיתוֹת as attributed, leaving the sages’ views in conflict.
steps.terutzMaskana: As a proposed reconciliation, switch the attributions in the later בָּרַיְיתָא.

steps.title: Why change the later teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the choice to reverse the later בָּרַיְיתָא rather than the earlier one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did you decide to reverse the later teaching? Reverse the earlier one instead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proposed fix. It asks what reason there is to correct the later בָּרַיְיתָא specifically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Switching the names in either בָּרַיְיתָא could remove the contradiction. Without a reason to prefer one source over the other, the proposed correction has not yet been justified.

phrases.english: What made you reverse the later teaching?
Reverse the earlier one instead!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the unsupported choice of which בָּרַיְיתָא to correct.
steps.kashyaTarget: The instruction to reverse the attributions in the later בָּרַיְיתָא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reversing the earlier בָּרַיְיתָא would also reconcile the two sources, so a reason is needed to choose the later one.

steps.title: Why the later ברייתא is the one reversed
steps.stepSummary: The later ברייתא is reversed because רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is known to hold that a whole house counts like four אמות. That makes him the strict opinion here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is known to say that an entire house is treated like four cubits? That is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the previous step: why reverse the later ברייתא and not the earlier one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds elsewhere that a whole house counts as one small area of four אמות. If so, moving the item behind the bed does not separate it from you, because it is still in the same 'four אמות'. So the strict opinion must be his, which matches the earlier ברייתא, and the later ברייתא is the one with the names switched.

keyTerms.meaning: You heard him (i.e., whom do we know holds this?)
Four cubits, a person's immediate personal area

phrases.english: Who have you heard who says
that an entire house is considered like four cubits?
It is Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.
phrases.notes: His view is known from the laws of עירובין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 42.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Consistency with the תנא's known position elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either ברייתא could have been the one with the names reversed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later ברייתא is reversed, because רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's known view (the whole house is like four אמות) makes him the strict one.

steps.title: How high must the bed be for the item under it to count as put away?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asked רב הונא: under three טפחים, the bed counts as connected to the ground (לבוד). What is the law for three through nine?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I asked רב הונא. A bed less than three handbreadths off the ground is obviously treated as connected to the ground. What about three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine handbreadths?
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier we learned that placing the item under the bed is enough. Now רב יוסף asks how high a bed can be off the floor and still work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of less than three טפחים is treated as if closed (לבוד). So an item under a very low bed is fully covered, as if hidden away. The open question is what happens when the gap is three to nine טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: A gap under three טפחים, treated as closed

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I asked Rav Huna:
A bed less than three handbreadths high
is obvious to me that it is considered connected (לבוד).
Three, four, five,
six, seven, eight,
nine, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new practical question about the 'under the bed' option from step 38.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an item under a bed raised three to nine טפחים count as put away?

steps.title: I don't know, but ten is clear
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answered that he did not know. רב יוסף adds that he never had a question about ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I don't know. About ten handbreadths, I certainly had no question.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא admits he has no answer for three to nine. Then רב יוסף notes that ten was never in doubt for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question stays open. The added line marks the upper boundary: at ten טפחים the case is clear, so the doubt is only between three and ten.

keyTerms.meaning: I have no question about it

phrases.english: He said to him: I do not know.
About ten I certainly had no question.
phrases.notes: Most likely רב יוסף speaking, since אביי (his student) answers him next. Sefaria reads it as רב הונא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question in step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no answer for three to nine. Ten is not in doubt.

steps.title: אביי confirms that ten is a separate domain
steps.stepSummary: אביי praises the reasoning: anything ten טפחים high is a separate domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You did well not to have a question, because anything ten handbreadths high is a separate domain.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the reason why ten טפחים was never in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten טפחים is the standard height that creates a separate רשות. So an item under a bed that high is in its own domain, apart from the room. That is why it is clearly fine.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You did well
that you had no question,
since anything ten handbreadths is a separate domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the 'ten is clear' statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten טפחים creates a separate domain.

steps.title: רבא sums up the bed-height rules
steps.stepSummary: Under three טפחים counts as לבוד. Ten is a separate domain. Three to ten is the unresolved question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The law is that less than three counts as connected. Ten is a separate domain. From three to ten is what רב יוסף asked רב הונא, and he did not resolve it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gathers the whole discussion into one clear summary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ends are settled: a very low bed and a ten-טפחים bed both work. The middle range stays an open question.

keyTerms.meaning: And he did not resolve it for him

steps.whatToRemember: Under 3 = לבוד (fine). 10 = separate domain (fine). 3 to 10 = unresolved.

phrases.english: Rava said: The law is,
less than three is considered connected.
Ten is a separate domain.
From three to ten:

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דִּבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף מֵרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: this is what Rav Yosef asked Rav Huna
and he did not resolve it for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizes steps 44 to 46.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under three טפחים and ten טפחים are both settled. Three to ten remains in doubt.

steps.title: רב and others rule like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב, and רב יעקב the son of שמואל's daughter (reported by באלי), rule that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The law follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. And so too, באלי said in the name of רב יעקב, son of שמואל's daughter: The law follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main dispute and brings rulings that side with the strict view of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this ruling, the whole room counts like four אמות. Moving the item behind the bed is not enough; it must be taken out or put under the bed.

phrases.english: Rav said:
The law follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.
And so too Bali said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יַעֲקֹב בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: that Rav Ya'akov, son of Shmuel's daughter, said:
The law follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the bed-height side discussion to rule on the main dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: רבא rules against רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees and rules that the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The law does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite ruling, so the final הלכה is now in dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, the room is not treated as one four-אמות area. Moving the item behind the bed is therefore enough.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same רבא who summarized the bed-height rules. Here he is ruling on a different question: the main dispute about רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: And Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: The law does not follow Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling of step 48.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: רב אחאי finds a ספר תורה in his son's wedding room
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי's son could not consummate his marriage. רב אחאי found a ספר תורה in the room and said they had endangered his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי arranged a marriage for his son into the family of רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא. He brought him into the חופה, but things did not succeed. He followed him to check, saw a ספר תורה lying there, and said to them: Had I not come now, you would have endangered my son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows a related law: the respect owed to a ספר תורה in a bedroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son's failure was taken as a sign that something improper was in the room. Having marital relations in front of an exposed ספר תורה is forbidden, and here it was even treated as dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: He arranged a marriage for his son

phrases.english: Rav Aḥai arranged a marriage for his son

phrases.aramaic: בֵּי רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא,
phrases.english: into the family of Rav Yitzḥak bar Shmuel bar Marta,
he brought him into the wedding canopy,
but the matter did not succeed.
He went after him to investigate,
he saw a Torah scroll lying there.
He said to them:
Had I not come now,
you would have endangered my son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a related law about holy objects in a room, told through a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An exposed ספר תורה in the room makes marital relations improper and even dangerous.

steps.title: The ברייתא behind רב אחאי's reaction
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids marital relations in a room with a ספר תורה or תפילין unless they are removed or placed in a כלי בתוך כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: In a room with a ספר תורה or תפילין, it is forbidden to have marital relations until one takes them out or puts them in a container inside another container.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב אחאי's complaint with a ברייתא that states the law clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to fix the problem: take the items out of the room, or double-cover them. One container is not enough for this stricter situation; it must be a container inside a container.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Phylacteries: boxes holding פסוקים, worn on the arm and head

steps.whatToRemember: With a ספר תורה or תפילין in the room, marital relations require removing them or placing them in a כלי בתוך כלי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה about holy objects in a bedroom.

phrases.english: As it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: בַּיִת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה אוֹ תְּפִילִּין
phrases.english: A room that has in it a Torah scroll or tefillin,
it is forbidden to have marital relations in it
until he takes them out
or places them in a container inside a container.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: בַּיִת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב אחאי's statement in step 50.
steps.raayaObject: רב אחאי's claim that the exposed ספר תורה was a serious problem
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding marital relations in a room with a ספר תורה or תפילין unless they are removed or placed in a כלי בתוך כלי

steps.title: אביי: the item's own regular container does not count as an extra layer
steps.stepSummary: אביי limits the ברייתא. A כלי בתוך כלי only works when at least one container is not the regular container of the ספר תורה or תפילין. Ten regular containers still count as only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The ברייתא only taught that two containers are enough when one container is not their regular one. But if all of them are their regular containers, even ten containers are treated like one container.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the ברייתא from step 51 more precisely. He limits when a כלי בתוך כלי is good enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said two layers of covering are enough. אביי adds that a container made for the ספר תורה or תפילין counts as part of the item itself, so stacking many of them does not help. You need a second container that is not their usual one.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught (this ruling) in the case of... (a formula that limits an earlier source)
A container inside a container (a double covering)
Their own container, the one regularly used for them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think more layers automatically help. If every layer is the item's normal container, even ten of them count as only one layer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule. A תפילין bag inside another תפילין bag is not enough. A different, outside container is needed.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They only taught (that a vessel within a vessel suffices)
in a vessel that is not their (regular) vessel,
but in a vessel that is their (regular) vessel —
even ten vessels
are considered like one vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the ברייתא's allowance of כלי בתוך כלי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלי בתוך כלי only counts when at least one container is not the item's regular container. Regular containers, however many, count as one.

steps.title: רבא begins a ruling about a cloak
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins a statement about a cloak (גלימא). The rest of his statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A cloak...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up the next move. רבא starts a new ruling about a cloak, and his full statement continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After אביי's rule about containers, רבא turns to a related practical case: covering with a garment. We will only see what he rules about it in the next part of the text.

phrases.english: Rava said: A cloak
phrases.notes: Statement continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related practical ruling about a garment, following אביי's rule about containers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incomplete on this amud. רבא begins a ruling about a cloak.
